en: The Apadāna of the Elder Bhisadāyaka Sakacintaniya Chapter, Number 5 I was once a physician, skilled in the knowledge of medicinal herbs. Seeing a monk who was ill, I gave him a *bhiṣa* (medicinal root). Because of that gift, I attained the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpatti-phala*). Having reached the state of a stream-enterer, I have now been reborn in heaven. There, I am honored by the gods; I am beautiful, possessing great splendor. I dwell in the company of the gods, enjoying celestial pleasures. By means of this gift of a *bhiṣa*, I have attained such a state. May I also attain the supreme, unsurpassed enlightenment. May I become a Buddha, a knower of all things, a teacher of the Dhamma. May I be one who brings happiness to the world, including the gods. May I be one who brings welfare to the world, including the gods. May I be one who brings bliss to the world, including the gods. May I be one who brings liberation to the world, including the gods. May I be one who brings security to the world, including the gods. May I be one who brings nirvāṇa to the world, including the gods. May I be one who brings peace to the world, including the gods. May I be one who brings cessation to the world, including the gods. May I be one who brings the end of suffering to the world, including the gods.

“Vessabhū by name was the third among the seers;
having entered the forest and the woods,”
The Supreme Person dwelt there.
Taking lotus roots and stalks,
I went into the presence of the Buddha.
And with my own hands, full of faith, I gave that to the Buddha;
and it was touched by his hand.
By Vessabhū of supreme wisdom:
"I do not know of any happiness equal to that;
how could there be anything superior?"
This is my final existence;
all states of being have been utterly uprooted by the peaceful Elephant-King.
Wholesome merit was planted by me.
That deed which I performed back then, thirty-one eons ago;
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of giving lotus roots.
And through the accumulation [of merit], kings—
There were sixteen lords of men;
in the [present] aeon,
there were fourteen wheel-turning monarchs of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Bhisadāyaka spoke these verses.
This is the fifth legend of the elder Bhisadāyaka.
